memos.headline: Rotation into Defensives and Cyclicals Accelerates as MSFT and AMZN Break Down; XOM and CAT Lead
memos.body: I see a sharply bifurcated tape today. On the strong side, CAT is trading within 0.1% of its 52-week high with RSI at 73.5 and +85.9% over 26 weeks—parabolic but undeniably the strongest relative-strength name in the universe at +37.8% vs SPY over 12 weeks. XOM is similarly powerful, +26.1% over 12 weeks with relative strength of +23.7% vs SPY and only -4.6% from highs. On the weak side, AMZN's RSI of 23.1 and -21.7% drawdown signal a broken chart with no sign of a base forming; MSFT at RSI 32.4 and -26.0% from highs is in a confirmed downtrend, trading nearly 18% below its 200-day mean. I have high conviction in the XOM uptrend and in avoiding MSFT and AMZN until they reclaim their 50-day averages; CAT's trend is extraordinary but the extension makes me cautious about chasing here—I'd need a pullback to the 50-day area (~634) to add with confidence.

views.note: Strongest relative strength in the universe (+23.7% vs SPY 12w), above both moving averages, RSI 65 not yet extreme; would reassess on a close below 135.
Parabolic trend with +85.9% 26w return and near all-time highs, but RSI 73.5 and +22% above 50d mean warn of mean-reversion risk; a close below 700 would change my view.
Steady uptrend with +12.2% relative strength vs SPY over 4 weeks, low ATR of 1.82%, and RSI 70 just reaching overbought—defensive leadership intact; would exit below 150.
Confirmed downtrend: -26% from 52w high, -17.7% below 200d mean, RSI 32.4, and -23.3% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks; no reason to step in until price reclaims 450.
Deeply oversold RSI 23.1 in a falling-knife pattern, -21.7% drawdown, -15% relative strength vs SPY over 4 weeks; need to see a base form above 200 before reconsidering.
Consolidating near the 50d mean with RSI 47.3 and modest -4.4% relative weakness over 12 weeks; no clear directional signal—would go long on a breakout above 195.
Long-term trend still positive (+51.8% 26w, +25.9% above 200d) but short-term RSI 32.3 pullback is sharp; watching 295 as support—a hold there could be a buying opportunity.
Sitting above the 200d mean (+6.5%) but below the 50d (-4.4%) with RSI 39.4 after a sharp -8% weekly drop; need to see 250 hold or I'd shift to avoid.
Mild pullback to RSI 41.8 with price still near the 200d mean (+1.9%) and only -9.6% from highs; inline with SPY, no edge either way—would get interested on a bounce above 310.
Despite a +6% bounce this week, the -51.1% drawdown from 52w high and -8.5% below the 200d mean indicate severe structural damage; would need a sustained move above 320 to reconsider.

memos.headline: MSFT and NVDA Deliver Exceptional Earnings Power; UNH Margin Collapse and XOM Revenue Decline Warrant Caution
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in MSFT and NVDA right now. MSFT posted 2026Q2 revenue of $81.27B (+16.7% YoY) with a stunning 47.3% net margin and net income growth of +59.5% YoY on only $40.26B of total debt—operating leverage is clearly inflecting higher. NVDA's 2026Q3 quarter showed $57.01B in revenue (+62.5% YoY) at a 56.0% net margin with minimal debt of $8.47B, though the data is now a quarter stale and I'd want to see the January-quarter filing before adding conviction. On the negative side, UNH's net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to $2.35B on a razor-thin 2.1% net margin against $80.14B of debt—this is cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for until I see a credible margin recovery path. XOM's revenue fell 5.2% YoY with net income down 12.3%, and at an 8.8% net margin the earnings trajectory is clearly negative absent a commodity price reversal.

views.note: Net income +59.5% YoY with 47.3% net margin and moderate $40.26B debt signals durable, expanding earnings power; would reassess if cloud segment growth decelerates below 20%.

62.5% YoY revenue growth and 56.0% net margin on minimal debt are extraordinary, but the most recent filing is from October 2025 so I discount conviction until the next quarter confirms sustainability.
Revenue +18.0% YoY to $113.83B with 30.3% net margin and only $14.79B debt is a strong combination; net income +29.8% shows operating leverage, and I'd stay long unless ad revenue growth stalls.
Revenue +15.7% YoY to $143.76B with 29.3% net margin is solid, though $88.50B of total debt is the highest in the tech cohort and I'd want to see services mix continue expanding.

Revenue +13.6% YoY is healthy but net income grew only 5.9% and the 9.9% net margin with $68.84B debt suggests margin expansion is stalling; would turn positive if operating income growth re-accelerates.
Revenue +8.8% and net income +11.6% YoY are respectable for a bank, but the data is from September 2025 and $427.20B of total debt makes the credit cycle the key swing factor.
Revenue grew only 1.5% YoY with net income declining 6.7%, yielding a 19.4% net margin—stable but not compelling enough to own when top-line growth is essentially flat.
Revenue +9.5% YoY but net income -6.7% signals margin pressure at 13.0%; I need to see the Q4 filing to determine if this is cyclical or structural before taking a directional view.
Net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to a 2.1% net margin on $80.14B of debt—this is severe cash-flow compression and I will not pay for it until margins demonstrably recover.
Revenue -5.2% and net income -12.3% YoY with an 8.8% net margin reflect commodity headwinds; would reconsider only if upstream realizations stabilize and downstream margins improve.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Intact With Moderating Inflation and Soft Labor Market – Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth Over Cyclicals
memos.body: I see a clear mid-cycle easing regime: the Fed has cut 75bp over the past year to a 3.75% upper bound, the 10y yield has fallen 48bp YoY to 4.04%, and the 2s10s curve has steepened 36bp to +0.62pp, all consistent with an ongoing normalization. CPI is running at 2.7% YoY – still above target but the 3m annualized pace (~2.4%) suggests continued disinflation, which should keep the Fed on a gradual cutting path. The unemployment rate at 4.30% is up 30bp YoY but ticked down 10bp over the last three months, pointing to a softening but not collapsing labor market. This backdrop favors duration-sensitive growth equities (tech) and is constructive for banks via a steeper curve, while I am less enthusiastic on pure cyclicals given the labor market slack and on energy given the demand implications of slower growth. A hot January CPI print (due soon) or a sudden spike in unemployment above 4.5% would force me to revisit this call.

views.note: Duration-sensitive mega-cap growth benefits directly from falling long rates and continued Fed easing; strong secular positioning.
Lower discount rates and easing financial conditions support premium consumer tech multiples in a soft-landing scenario.
High-duration growth name that benefits from rate declines, though elevated valuation warrants slightly lower conviction.
Steepening 2s10s curve (+36bp YoY to +0.62pp) supports net interest margins; easing cycle historically positive for credit quality.
Consumer spending resilient with unemployment only 4.3%; falling rates support both growth multiple and AWS capex financing.
Defensive staples less compelling when growth equities benefit from falling rates; 2.7% CPI still pressures input costs.
Cyclical exposure is mixed – easing helps capex financing but rising unemployment YoY signals softening industrial demand.
Slowing growth backdrop and rising unemployment suggest weaker energy demand; macro regime does not favor commodity cyclicals.
Ad-driven revenue benefits from still-positive consumer spending; lower rates support growth multiples broadly.
Defensive healthcare less rate-sensitive; macro regime neither strongly supports nor undermines the name.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: UNH and MSFT Crushed, CAT and PG Quietly Positive
memos.body: I am reading the earnings-season price reactions as sentiment proxies given the absence of granular GDELT tone data in this evidence set. The standout negative reactions were UNH (-19.6% on 1/27) and MSFT (-10.0% on 1/29), both of which suggest a sharp narrative deterioration that may not yet be fully digested—UNH in particular looks like a regime-change event in sentiment. On the positive side, CAT (+3.4% on 1/29) and PG (+2.6% on 1/22) posted solid post-earnings gains, indicating constructive tone that could build further if macro narratives cooperate. AMZN's -5.6% drop on 2/6 is fresh and likely still being processed by the market, while AAPL (+0.5%), GOOGL (-0.5%), and XOM (+0.6%) were essentially non-events, suggesting sentiment is already priced in for those names.

views.note: A -19.6% post-earnings collapse signals a severe negative narrative shift that likely has further to run as media coverage catches up.
A -10.0% earnings-day drop is a major sentiment reset; I expect negative tone to persist near-term before any stabilization.
A +3.4% post-earnings pop with governance changes suggests improving narrative momentum in industrials.
Steady +2.6% post-earnings gain and multiple Reg FD disclosures point to a constructive, under-the-radar positive tone.
Fresh -5.6% earnings reaction just a week old means negative sentiment is still being absorbed and could weigh further.
A muted +0.5% earnings reaction suggests sentiment is balanced and already priced; no edge here.
A -0.5% post-earnings move is noise, not signal; sentiment appears fully priced.
A +0.6% post-earnings move is negligible; no clear sentiment direction to trade.
The -4.2% earnings drop on 1/13 was notable but a month of subsequent filings without further price shock suggests sentiment has stabilized.
Only a board-level personnel change on file with no earnings reaction data; insufficient signal to take a directional view.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Near Historic Highs Signals Structural Geopolitical Risk Across Export-Sensitive and Energy Names
memos.body: I am flagging a dramatic surge in the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index to 438.29, up 95.3% over three months and 55.6% in the last month alone, coinciding with a VIX spike to 20.82 (+37.7% 1m). This combination points to an escalation in trade-policy, sanctions, or export-control actions rather than a garden-variety macro scare—credit spreads (HY OAS at 2.92%) have barely moved, suggesting the stress is concentrated in policy channels, not broad credit deterioration. WTI crude at $63.08 is firming (+6.2% 1m), which I read as supply-side tightening consistent with sanctions enforcement or OPEC discipline rather than demand-driven strength. For the portfolio, I see the most direct geopolitical exposure in NVDA (China export controls), CAT (tariff and infrastructure-spend sensitivity), XOM (energy-security beneficiary), and PG (FX/tariff pass-through risk on global consumer goods). I would need to see a concrete de-escalation in trade or export-control policy—such as a formal waiver or bilateral agreement—to upgrade the names I currently flag as vulnerable.

views.note: Extreme policy uncertainty at 438 likely reflects tightening semiconductor export controls to China, which directly constrains NVDA's data-center TAM; no evidence of waivers or relief.
WTI firming to $63 amid geopolitical supply tightening benefits XOM's upstream margins; two recent Reg FD filings suggest active investor communication around the energy-security theme.
CAT is a two-way bet—tariffs raise input costs but infrastructure-spend mandates could offset; the Jan 29 Reg FD filing may address guidance but I lack detail to take a directional view.

Surging policy uncertainty and potential tariff escalation pressure PG's global supply chain and FX-sensitive margins; two Reg FD filings in January suggest management is actively managing expectations.

Banks benefit from steeper curves (10y-2y at +0.62) but elevated policy uncertainty and three 8-K filings in five weeks suggest JPM is navigating a complex regulatory or deal environment; net effect unclear.
Apple's China manufacturing concentration makes it highly exposed to the policy-uncertainty spike; no offsetting evidence of supply-chain diversification in the filing record.

plan.summary: Elevated policy uncertainty and a bifurcated tape favor a barbell of defensive momentum (XOM, PG) and high-quality growth names where fundamentals are strongest (GOOGL), with a modest allocation to JPM on curve steepening. We hold ~35% cash to buffer against the VIX spike and historic policy uncertainty readings.

plans.rationale: Strongest relative strength in the universe per Technical (+23.7% vs SPY 12w), geopolitical supply tightening supports upstream margins per Geopolitics, and sentiment was a non-event post-earnings. Fundamentals flag declining earnings but the macro energy-security bid and technical momentum dominate near-term.
plans.changes_my_mind: A weekly close below 135 (the 50-day support area) or WTI crude falling below $58 would invalidate the supply-tightening thesis.

plans.rationale: Technical shows steady defensive leadership with +12.2% relative strength vs SPY over 4 weeks and low ATR. Sentiment is constructive post-earnings (+2.6%). Fundamentals are uninspiring (flat revenue) and Geopolitics flags tariff risk, so I size modestly. Net, the defensive rotation theme and technical trend win.
plans.changes_my_mind: A weekly close below 150 or evidence of tariff-driven margin compression in upcoming guidance.

plans.rationale: Fundamentals are strong: +18% revenue growth, 30.3% net margin, low debt per Fundamentals analyst (0.80 conviction). Macro supports duration-sensitive growth via falling rates. Technical shows a sharp short-term pullback (RSI 32.3) within a positive long-term trend (+51.8% 26w), offering a potential entry. Sentiment was neutral post-earnings. I size moderately given the short-term weakness.
plans.changes_my_mind: A weekly close below 295 (Technical's key support) or ad revenue growth decelerating below 10% in next quarter.

plans.rationale: Macro analyst highlights steepening 2s10s curve (+36bp YoY) supporting NIM, and fundamentals show solid +11.6% net income growth. Technical is neutral with a mild pullback, and sentiment has stabilized after the initial earnings dip. Geopolitical uncertainty and high policy-uncertainty index keep this a smaller position.
plans.changes_my_mind: A close below 280 or a flattening of the 2s10s spread back below +0.30pp.

orders.note: Defensive momentum, low vol, tight gaps, flat 1w return — no reason to delay; market_open fill with modest gap guard.
Staples name with smallest avg gap and low ATR/price (~1.8%). Steady mover, want to be filled. Gap guard at 3%.
Down >5% in the past week with elevated ATR (~3.6% of price) and large avg gaps. Use a limit ~$5.47 below close (299.25 area) to capture continued weakness; skip if it gaps up >4%.

execution.notes: Defensive names (XOM, PG) get market_open for reliable fills. Extended or recently volatile names (GOOGL, JPM, CAT) get limit entries to improve execution price. 35% cash buffer already in plan provides cushion.
